items: Show a small portfolio of case studies: problem, process, result and honest impact.
Sell clear packages with scope, revision rounds and timelines.
Agree everything in writing and take an advance payment before starting.
Refuse fees to get work, overpayment refunds and huge unpaid tests; stay on the platform until trust is built.
Respect copyright and licences for photos, fonts and stock elements; check the current terms.
Create original logos and get consent for photos of real people.

cards.prompt: Write a short description of your first design package: what is included, how many revisions, how long it takes and what you need from the client. Then list three red flags that would make you say no to a client.

quiz.question: What makes a portfolio case study strong?
options: It shows the problem, the process and the result
It shows as many images as possible with no words
It lists software you have installed
It includes other designers' best work
quiz.explanation: Clients want to see how you think and what your work achieved, not just pretty pictures.

quiz.question: A 'client' asks you to pay a registration fee before giving you design work. What is this most likely to be?
options: A normal step for every design job
A tax required by the platform
A way to unlock better templates
A scam
quiz.explanation: Genuine clients pay designers; they do not charge designers to work. A fee to get work is a classic scam sign.

quiz.question: Why is a photo from a search engine not automatically free to use in a client's ad?
options: Someone usually owns it, so you need permission
Search engine photos are always too small to print
Photos online are free once they are a year old
Only printed photos are protected by copyright
quiz.explanation: Being easy to download does not make a photo free. Use your own photos, the client's photos or properly licensed images.

quiz.question: Zoya wants her new logo built from a stock graphic in the design tool. What is the main concern?
options: Stock graphics cannot be resized once they are placed in a design
Licences may limit stock elements in logos
Logos must always be black and white
Stock graphics only work on printed items
quiz.explanation: Stock elements are shared by many users and their licences often limit trademark use. An original logo is safer for the client. Always check the current licence terms.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a watermark on design drafts?
options: To improve the colours of the design
To show which template was used
To stop drafts being used before final payment
To make the file print faster
quiz.explanation: Watermarked or low-resolution previews let clients review drafts while protecting your work until they pay.

quiz.question: A new client sends more money than agreed and asks you to send back the difference quickly. What should you do?
options: Refund the difference straight away to be polite
Keep the extra money as a tip
Ask them to send even more next time
Wait until the payment clears before any refund
quiz.explanation: Overpayment tricks rely on you refunding before the first payment bounces or is reversed. Wait and verify through your bank or platform.

quiz.question: What does 'scope' mean in a design agreement?
options: The client's favourite colour
The zoom level of the design
The number of fonts in a template
The exact work included in the agreed price
quiz.explanation: Scope defines what is included, such as the number of posts and sizes, so both sides know what extra work means.

quiz.question: You want to post a photo of a customer's child enjoying a cake on the bakery's page. What is required first?
options: A higher resolution version of the photo
A brighter filter so the child looks happier
Permission from the parent or guardian
Nothing, because the photo was taken in the shop
quiz.explanation: Photos of recognisable people, especially children, need consent before they are used in public or commercial posts.

quiz.question: Which is the best way to set your first design package price?
options: Consider scope, hours, value to the client and similar local offers
Copy the cheapest price you can find online
Charge the same for a logo and a single post
Never set a price and let each client decide what they think the work is worth
quiz.explanation: A sensible price reflects the work, the use and the value. Racing to the bottom makes your business hard to sustain.

quiz.question: Which practice keeps a freelance project calm and professional?
options: Starting immediately without any discussion
Agreeing scope, revisions, timeline, payment and rights in writing
Keeping all terms verbal to stay flexible
Delivering final files before any payment is agreed
quiz.explanation: Written agreements prevent misunderstandings and give both sides a fair way to handle extra requests.

bank.question: A poster has a large headline, a large photo and a large price, all in bold red. The squint test shows no clear focus. What is the best next step?
options: Add a bold red border so all three are framed together
Make the background red too so everything matches
Pick one winner and tone down the other two
Increase all three sizes equally until they touch
bank.explanation: Hierarchy needs one clear winner. When several elements use every tool of emphasis at once, none stands out. Reduce emphasis on the supporting items.

bank.question: Which change most improves the readability of white text placed over a busy, colourful photo?
options: Add a dark, semi-transparent overlay behind the text
Change the text to a thin script font
Make the text much smaller so it covers less of the photo
Add more colours to the text so it matches the photo
bank.explanation: An overlay calms the busy photo and increases contrast, so the text becomes easy to read while the photo still shows.

bank.question: Ayesha's flyer uses a serif heading font, a sans-serif body font and a script font for 'Eid Mubarak'. Which statement is most accurate?
options: It must fail because more than one font is never allowed
Script fonts are best for body text, so swap them
Serif and sans-serif fonts can never appear together
It works if the script is kept to those two big words
bank.explanation: Two main fonts plus a decorative accent used very sparingly can work. The risk is using script for small or long text.

bank.question: Why does moving a product name and its price close together, and away from the address, improve a menu?
options: It increases the contrast between the text colours
Proximity shows which details belong together
It makes the menu print with less ink
It creates repetition across different pages
bank.explanation: Items placed close together are read as a group. Separating unrelated items avoids confusion.

bank.question: A client says the redesigned poster 'looks too empty' after Ayesha added white space around the headline. Which reply best explains the design choice?
options: Empty areas reduce printing costs by using less ink
White space is required by printers for every poster
The space pulls attention to the offer
The space will be filled later by customers' notes
bank.explanation: White space is a tool for focus. It reduces competition around the main message and signals quality.

bank.question: Which combination is the strongest starting point for a calm, readable bakery poster?
options: Six bright colours with white text on each colour
Cream base, maroon headline, one gold accent
A neon green background with yellow text
A busy pattern background with grey body text
bank.explanation: A small palette with strong text contrast and one accent gives both mood and readability.

bank.question: Which description of alignment is correct?
options: Giving every element the same colour and font size
Rotating text so it fits diagonally across a page
Spacing every element exactly 1 cm from the next
Lining elements up along shared edges
bank.explanation: Alignment creates invisible connections between elements, which makes a design look organised.

bank.question: Hamza is choosing between templates. Which factor should matter most?
options: Whether the layout fits the amount of text and images he has
Whether the template photos are the ones he will finally use in the poster
Whether the template has the most decorative stickers
Whether the template appeared first in the search
bank.explanation: Text, photos and colours are easy to replace; a fitting structure is the hard part to rebuild.

bank.question: After adding a background photo, the headline disappears. Hamza types a new headline on top. Why is this a poor fix?
options: New text boxes cannot be downloaded
Canva allows only one text box on each page of a design, so it will fail
The old headline is still hidden behind, which can cause errors later
Typing a new headline deletes the photo
bank.explanation: The original is hidden in the layer order. Duplicate hidden elements lead to editing the wrong one. Use layer or position options instead.

bank.question: Which keyboard shortcut duplicates a selected element in Canva on Windows?
options: Ctrl + D
Ctrl + U
Ctrl + Shift + Q
Alt + Tab
bank.explanation: Ctrl + D (Cmd + D on Mac) duplicates the selected element in Canva. Alt + Tab switches between windows on Windows.

bank.question: Why is it wise to learn Canva features by their purpose rather than memorising exact button positions?
options: Every button in Canva is hidden until you pay
Buttons are the same in every design tool ever made
Shortcuts stop working after each update
Menus change between versions and plans differ
bank.explanation: Menus move and plans differ. Understanding what a feature does helps you find it again after updates.

bank.question: Hamza wants his logo and team name to move and resize together, while the background stays fixed. What should he do?
options: Lock the logo and name, and group the background layers
Group the logo and name, and lock the background
Duplicate the background and delete the logo
Change the logo and name to the same font
bank.explanation: Grouping joins elements so they move as one; locking stops an element from moving by accident.

bank.question: A template contains an element marked for paid plans and Ayesha uses a free plan. Which action respects the licence terms?
options: Take a screenshot of the element and paste it in
Download the design and crop out the watermark
Replace it with a free element or her own image
Find the same image on a search engine and use that
bank.explanation: Screenshots, cropping watermarks or using search-engine copies can break licence terms. Use free or own content.

bank.question: What is the main benefit of making a copy of a design before trying a new colour scheme?
options: The copy downloads at a higher resolution
The original stays safe for comparison
Copies unlock extra templates
It removes the need to proofread
bank.explanation: A copy is a free safety net for experiments, and side-by-side comparison helps decisions.

bank.question: A client wants one square image used unchanged as a story, a feed post and an A4 flyer. What is the most professional response?
options: Explain each place needs its own layout and adapt
Agree, because colours matter more than shapes
Stretch the square to each new shape
Send the square image and let each platform crop it
bank.explanation: Different shapes and viewing distances need different layouts. Resizing tools help, but each version should be checked and adjusted.

bank.question: Which headline is strongest for a weekend tasting flyer?
options: Qureshi Sweets and Bakers Is Pleased To Invite All Families
Information
Please Read The Details Below Carefully
Free Rusk Tasting
bank.explanation: A short headline states the main message in a few words and can be read from a distance.

bank.question: A story design has the call to action at the very bottom edge. What is the main risk?
options: The story will be rejected for being too large
App buttons or reply bars may cover it
Bottom text always appears in black and white
The story cannot be shared by others
bank.explanation: Story screens show interface elements near the top and bottom. Keep key text in the central safe area.

bank.question: Which statement about A4 and US Letter is correct?
options: A4 and US Letter are exactly the same size
US Letter is the standard paper size in Pakistan
A4 is 210 x 297 mm; US Letter differs slightly
A4 is 148 x 210 mm and used mainly for posters
bank.explanation: A4 is 210 x 297 mm and standard in Pakistan and most countries. US Letter is 216 x 279 mm. 148 x 210 mm is A5.

bank.question: A social post has a long address and opening hours in tiny text across the bottom. What is the best fix?
options: Make the text thinner so it takes less room
Spread the details across all four corners
Add a second address in a different font
Move the details into the caption
bank.explanation: Images carry the main message; captions hold details people may want to read or copy.

bank.question: Which check is most important before sending 1,000 flyers to print?
options: Checking numbers and dates with a second reader
Changing the font one last time
Adding a few more decorations
Lowering the image quality to make the file smaller
bank.explanation: Errors in numbers and dates are the most costly mistakes in print. A second reader catches what you miss.

bank.question: Why do the rusk post and flyer look like a pair?
options: They repeat the same photo, colours and fonts
They were printed on the same day
They use exactly the same dimensions
They both include the full menu and prices
bank.explanation: Repetition of visual choices builds recognition across different formats.

bank.question: A brand palette lists gold as the accent. A new designer uses gold for the background, headline and buttons. What is the main problem?
options: Gold cannot be printed on any paper
Accent colours are only for logos
Gold always lowers text contrast on cream
The accent stops standing out
bank.explanation: An accent works by being used sparingly. Overusing it removes the contrast that makes key actions stand out.

bank.question: Bilal's nephew stretched the logo and changed its colour for a Ramadan post. What is the best long-term solution?
options: Adopt a new logo each season to stay fresh
Allow anyone to change the logo if the owner likes it
Keep the approved logo and add seasonal elements around it
Use the stretched logo for print and the original for posts
bank.explanation: The logo stays fixed so people always recognise it. Seasonal variety belongs in photos, accents and graphics.

bank.question: Which item does NOT normally belong in a simple brand guide?
options: Exact colour codes and their roles
A list of the owner's personal passwords
Heading and body fonts with sizes
Logo versions and clear space rules
bank.explanation: A brand guide covers colours, fonts, logos, photo style and voice. Passwords never belong in a shared design document.

bank.question: A business's plan does not include a brand kit. Which approach still gives strong consistency?
options: Choosing colours by eye for each new design
Letting each staff member pick fonts they like
Avoiding logos so there is nothing to keep consistent
A short brand guide plus master templates
bank.explanation: Consistency comes from clear rules and ready-styled templates, which work on any plan.

bank.question: In the 'Where is your brand today?' matrix, which describes a feed where every post grabs attention but nobody links them to one business?
options: Strong brand
Eye-catching chaos
Consistent but dull
Invisible
bank.explanation: High impact with low consistency is eye-catching chaos. A strong brand combines impact with consistency.

bank.question: A menu marks sold-out items only by turning them red. Why is this a weak choice?
options: Some readers cannot easily tell colours apart
Red ink costs more than other colours
Red is never allowed in food brands
Colour changes stop the menu from being saved as PDF
bank.explanation: Do not rely on colour alone. Add a word or icon, such as 'Sold out', so everyone understands.

bank.question: Why is the white version of a logo placed on a dark maroon background, rather than the maroon version?
options: Because white logos always print sharper
Because maroon logos are only for videos
So the logo keeps enough contrast to stay visible
Because dark backgrounds always require a stretched logo
bank.explanation: Approved light and dark versions ensure the logo is always visible against its background.

bank.question: A printer says Bilal's flyer will show white edges after cutting. What setting is missing?
options: A higher number of fonts
A transparent background behind every page of the flyer
A GIF animation
Bleed past the trim line
bank.explanation: Bleed extends the background beyond the cut line so small cutting shifts do not reveal white paper.

bank.question: A fresh graduate's CV is three pages with skills shown as coloured bars. Which change gives the biggest improvement?
options: Add more colours to the bars for each skill
Cut to one or two pages and describe skills in text with evidence
Convert the whole CV into one large image so the layout never moves when opened
Use a script font so it looks creative
bank.explanation: Recruiters scan quickly and software may read CVs. Short, clear text with evidence beats graphics.

bank.question: Which export choice is most suitable for a printed brochure going to a professional printer?
options: A print-quality PDF with bleed and crop marks if the printer asks
A small JPG sent through a messaging app, since printers can enlarge any picture
A GIF so the pages can loop
A screenshot of the design on a phone
bank.explanation: Printers usually want a print-quality PDF with their requested settings. Always confirm with the printer.

bank.question: A 15-second animated ad shows the logo for 10 seconds before the product appears. What is the main weakness?
options: Logos are not allowed in animated ads
15 seconds is too short to export
The hook and product come too late
Animations cannot include products
bank.explanation: Short feed videos need a hook and the product early. The logo can close the ad with the call to action.

bank.question: Which pairing of file type and use is correct?
options: GIF for a printed A4 flyer
MP4 for an animated post with sound
JPG for a logo that needs a transparent background
PDF for a looping silent sticker
bank.explanation: MP4 suits video and longer animation. GIFs are for short silent loops, PNG supports transparency, and PDF suits documents and print.

bank.question: A bright on-screen green looks duller on the printed proof. What best explains this?
options: Screens mix light (RGB); printers mix ink (CMYK)
The printer used the wrong paper size
Canva saves greens as black and white
The bleed area always changes every colour in the design when it is printed
bank.explanation: Some RGB colours fall outside what inks can print. A printed proof shows the real result before the full run.

bank.question: Which slide headline best follows professional presentation practice?
options: Research
Slide 4
Here is a lot of information about what we found during our research project
Young buyers find new brands on short videos
bank.explanation: A short sentence headline states the point of the slide so the audience gets the takeaway at once.

bank.question: Which portfolio entry is the most convincing to a potential client?
options: Fifty unrelated images with no explanation
Unchanged templates presented as original work
A case study of a bakery rebrand: problem, process, result
Screenshots of a famous agency's best campaigns, to show the style she likes most
bank.explanation: Case studies show thinking and impact. Presenting templates or others' work as your own is misleading.

bank.question: A new contact asks for a 20-post unpaid 'test', a joining fee and a move to WhatsApp. How many classic scam signs are present?
options: One
Three
Two
None
bank.explanation: A huge unpaid test, a fee to get work and pressure to leave the platform are each common scam signs.

bank.question: Zoya wants a logo she can register as a trademark. Which approach is safest?
options: A stock graphic from the design tool with her name added
A logo copied from a famous brand with new colours
An original logo, not built from stock graphics
A photo found online turned into a logo
bank.explanation: Stock elements are shared and their licences often limit trademark use. Copying a brand is infringement. Original work is safest; check the current licence terms.

bank.question: After two agreed revision rounds, a client asks for more changes. What does a good agreement allow?
options: Offering extra rounds at the rate stated in the agreement
Refusing all contact until the client accepts
Deleting the client's files
Doing unlimited free changes because the client is always right
bank.explanation: A written agreement makes extra work easy to discuss fairly and calmly.

bank.question: A client sends double the agreed advance and asks for half back urgently. What is the safest action?
options: Refund at once to show good faith
Spend the extra on stock images for the project
Ask the client to pay a third time
Wait until the payment has fully cleared
bank.explanation: Overpayment scams rely on a quick refund before the original payment is reversed.

bank.question: A bakery wants to post a photo of a regular customer's young son eating cake. What is the correct first step?
options: Blur the cake so the photo is more artistic
Post it, since it was taken inside the shop
Ask the parent or guardian for permission
Add a filter so the child is less recognisable
bank.explanation: Photos of recognisable people, especially children, need consent before public or commercial use.

bank.question: Which pricing approach is most sustainable for a new designer?
options: Always be the cheapest designer online
Charge the same for every type of job
Let each client decide the price after delivery, based on how happy they feel
Price by scope, time and value; raise it as you grow
bank.explanation: Pricing for scope and value keeps the business healthy. Racing to the bottom is hard to sustain.
